feedback: Pre-race review of the iteration 11 candidate, the final iteration. It keeps the iteration 9 and 10 design (narrow five-sensor array at x = 0.03, 0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03 with y = 0.05, sensor_size 0.016, sensor_weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], base_speed 1.1, kd 0.3, ki 0, last_direction) and changes one variable, kp from 1.8 to 1.6. The reason is the kp trend: iteration 6 (kp 2.5 to 2.0) cut oval line_loss_events from 0.95 to 0.85 and s-bend line loss from 1.25 to 1.1, and iteration 8 (kp 2.0 to 1.8) cut oval line loss from 0.85 to 0.30. The s-bend is still at line_loss_events 2.0 under the 16 mm footprint (iteration 9 and 10), so it is the clearest remaining gap. The candidate is valid and within contract limits, and it is not stacked with other changes. Nothing about its performance can be read from earlier races, so the race is the only real test. Approved so the single change is raced and the team has a scored design. The fallback is the iteration 10 design (kp 1.8, sensor_size 0.016), which is the best raced result at 403.3. If the race shows oval completion falling below 18 of 20, or oval max_error rising above 0.044, the tightest bends are being under-corrected and the kp 1.8 design is the one to race. Because this is the final iteration and the held-back race is scored once, the more robust choice is the one with the least risk on unseen tracks.
requested_changes: Race kp 1.6 with sensor_size 0.016, base_speed 1.1, kd 0.3, ki 0 and last_direction held. This tests whether the kp trend (2.5 to 2.0 to 1.8) continues to cut line loss on the s-bend, which stayed at 2.0 in iteration 9 and 10.

If the oval completion falls below 18 of 20 or oval max_error rises above 0.044 at kp 1.6, the fallback is kp 1.8 with sensor_size 0.016 (iteration 10, 403.3), since the tightest bends are being under-corrected.
Keep the five-sensor spacing and sensor_weights [2,1,0,-1,-2] unchanged, since iteration 2 (22.5 mm spacing) dropped the score to 81.1 and iteration 7 (kd 0.25) dropped it to 163.3.
